sections.content:
Interesting! After LEFT×5 (tip 46→16): red moved from (31,42) to (31,18) — followed the tip! But blue (19,42) and green (25,42) stayed at column 42!
So only the red (the block at the beam's row) is carried horizontally. Blue/green are not carried.
Wait, but at t38 all three moved up together. Now only the red follows the tip.
Revised model: the block at the beam's row (the "active" block, red) is carried by the beam (both row and column). The other blocks (blue, green) are... at t38 they moved up by 6. Why?
Ah. Maybe blue/green are "falling" or "stacking" on top of the red! The red is at (31,42), the green is at (31,42)?? No — before t38: red (37,42), green (31,42), blue (25,42). After t38: red (31,42), green (25,42), blue (19,42).
The red moved up by 6 (carried). The green moved up by 6, the blue moved up by 6. If the green/blue were just sitting on top of the red (a stack with a 6px pitch), then when the red was lifted, the stack would... no, if the red is lifted, the green/blue should fall (gravity) or stay put.
They moved up with the red. So they're attached to the red (a rigid stack) — but only vertically! Now, when the red moved left (column 42→18), the green/blue didn't follow horizontally.
So: the green/blue are attached to the red vertically (they move with the red's row) but not horizontally?? That's weird.
Or: the green/blue are attached to column 42 (the wall), and move vertically with the beam's row? At t38 the beam's row moved up by 6, and the green/blue moved up by 6. Now the beam's row hasn't changed (P=30), the red moved left, and the green/blue stayed.
Hmm, so the green/blue's row = the red's row - 6, -12 (a stack on top of the red), but the column is fixed at 42?
Let me test: move the player UP (beam's row -6). If the green/blue follow the red's row → they're attached to the red. Prediction: red (25,18), green (19,42), blue (13,42).
Or maybe the green/blue's row = the beam's row - 7, -13 (attached to the beam). Same prediction.
Test: UP once.

sections.content:
<tool_call>
<function=python>
<parameter=code>
def state(f):
    out={}
    for n in f.segmentation['nodes']:
        b=n['boundary']; rs=[p[0] for p in b]
        if n['color']=='M' and n['pixels']==18 and min(rs)<54: out['P']=min(rs)
        if n['color'] in ('R','b','N') and n['pixels']==16 and min(rs)<54:
            cs=[p[1] for p in b]; out[n['color']]=(min(rs),min(cs))
    return out
res = action(['UP'])
print('after UP:', state(current_frame))
</parameter>
</function>
</tool_call>
